$comment: DRAFT — not a shipped contract. Authority: docs/26-LOCATE-SCOPE.md §3.2 and §5, under North Star decision #30. Written from crates/ethos-parser-core/src/locate.rs; if the two disagree, the Rust is the implementation and the scope is the argument. Guarded by contract_invariants.rs::the_locations_schema_pins_the_version_and_rule_the_code_emits, because a schema without a guard drifts and the drift is invisible to exactly the reader the file is for.
title: ethos.parser.locations.v0
description: Where one string lies in one representation, and nothing else. There is no verdict here, no boolean, no score and no evidence tier: a string that occurs nowhere is this artifact with an empty `occurrences` array and the same exit code a found one has. Whether a location supports a claim stays the verifier's to say (docs/07-VERIFY-BOUNDARY.md §2), and this artifact has no claim input to answer it with. Every value in it is a COPY of something the representation already states — node ids verbatim, offsets into each node's own text, and the record's own geometry — which is what keeps it from becoming a second evidence tier.

parser_version.description: The engine build that answered. It is covered by `profile_sha256`, so that digest moves with every release and no two releases' artifacts are silently comparable.

profile_sha256.description: Profile-as-identity: two artifacts are comparable if and only if this matches. It covers `locate_rule`, so an answer produced under a different match rule is correctly non-comparable rather than quietly different.

source_sha256.description: The original source bytes, carried through from the representation.

representation_sha256.description: The representation that was searched — the binding that makes an occurrence checkable. It is verified BEFORE anything is searched: a record whose payload does not hash to its declared digest is not one this engine will speak for. NOTE that it does not cover the geometry below. Geometry sits outside the representation's fingerprint by design (docs/01-CONTRACT.md §4), and nobody should read this digest as covering a rectangle it never touched.

locate_rule.description: Which match rule produced this. `locate-scalar-exact-v1` is code-point-exact on Unicode scalars: no normalization, no case folding, no whitespace folding. A normalised or folded rule is a `-v2` with its own id, never a flag on this one (scope §4.1, §7).

quote_scalars.description: The quote's length in Unicode scalars — not UTF-8 bytes, not UTF-16 code units — so a consumer can check an offset range's width without holding the quote. The minimum is 1 because the empty quote is refused rather than answered: it occurs at every offset of every block, so *where it occurs* has no answer with a meaning.

searched.description: What the rule looked at, stated because it is LESS than the whole record. The rule searches each block of the reading-order cut, so a match may join runs inside one block and may not join across two — a block boundary is a gap the page drew. These three counts are how that narrowing is visible rather than silent (scope §11.1).

blocks.description: Blocks the cut grouped them into — the strings actually searched. A run a table already claims is its own block, so a cell's runs are one-member blocks and a cell's concatenated text is not searched by `-v1`.

occurrences.description: Every occurrence, in reading order, overlapping starts included: `aa` occurs twice in `aaa`. **Reading order is not a ranking** — nothing here prefers one occurrence to another. Empty when the string occurs nowhere, and empty when `occurrences_withheld` is present.

occurrences_withheld.description: Present only when the count passed the ceiling, in which case `occurrences` is empty and this carries the count. ALL of them are withheld, never the excess alone: a truncated list would locate some of a document's occurrences and silently drop the rest, which is the same shape of lie `SpansWithheld` refuses. The count still travels, because a count is one of the honest signals docs/00-NORTH-STAR.md §3 permits.

limit.description: The ceiling they passed: 1,000,000, which is `ethos.grounding.v1`'s own element ceiling. Measured at 127.6 MiB of artifact — docs/measurements/locate/README.md.

occurrence.title: Occurrence
occurrence.description: One place the string occurs. It carries no id of its own, no page and no union box: an occurrence is addressed by the node ids the record already minted, and minting a second id space for it is refused (scope §7, §11.2).

parts.description: One per node the occurrence's scalars touch, in order. **Their own slices, concatenated, equal the quote exactly** — the invariant that makes an occurrence re-resolvable, and the one that fails the moment an offset is written against the block's text instead of the node's.

synthesized.description: How many of this occurrence's scalars this reader synthesized rather than read — a space inserted for a gap the content stream drew, for instance. **Stated always, never omitted at zero**: a consumer matching a quote against a space the source does not contain is the failure docs/01-CONTRACT.md §10 names, and this is the field that can warn them.

occurrence_part.title: OccurrencePart
occurrence_part.description: One node's share of an occurrence.

node.description: The node id, copied verbatim out of the representation searched. An OPAQUE HANDLE: it travels back as the bytes the engine handed out, and one this engine did not mint fails closed (docs/history/12-V12-SCOPE.md §3).

char_start.description: First scalar of **this node's own `text`**, inclusive, in Unicode scalars — as `Span.char_start` is, and for the same reason: not bytes, not UTF-16 units.

char_end.description: One past the last scalar, exclusive.

geometry.description: That node's geometry, COPIED from the representation's sidecar rather than derived. No sub-run box and no word box: docs/22-WORD-BOXES-SCOPE.md §7 refused those on measurement, so an occurrence inside a run carries the run's own rectangle and nothing tighter.
